extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and readers evaluating bibliometric and science-mapping studies (and bibliometric researchers preparing manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for assessing bibliometric performance analysis and science-mapping (conceptual, intellectual, social structure) studies. Focuses on methodological choices, interpretation, integration of analyses, and limitations relevant to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify choice of field normalization method
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should clearly justify their choice of normalization method (e.g., mean-normalized citation score (MNCS), percentile-based normalization, source-normalized impact per paper (SNIP), time-window normalization approaches) and demonstrate its appropriateness for the specific research context, particularly when comparing research impact across different disciplines or periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why a given normalization (MNCS vs SNIP vs percentile vs time-window) was selected for the dataset and comparisons; discuss strengths/limitations (e.g., MNCS better for similar fields, SNIP for disparate disciplines) and show sensitivity to choice when interpreting cross-field or temporal comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for h-index limitations and career-stage bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The combination use of h-index can shed light on total citations but has limitations, including bias toward senior researchers with longer publication histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ensure studies acknowledge and adjust for h-index biases (e.g., by using article fractionalization, m-index, considering first year of publication to identify emerging scholars) and avoid direct comparisons across career stages without normalization or contextualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection threshold for 'top' lists must avoid arbitrary cutoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting ranking tables (top authors, journals, countries), researchers should justify the threshold to select top entities because common habits like top-ten lists may contain selection biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of arbitrary cutoffs (e.g., top 10) when adjacent ranks are similar; consider using a larger threshold (the article suggests top twelve) or statistical thresholds, and discuss sensitivity to chosen cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking and ranking criteria transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When authors and journals share the same number of productions, additional metrics (h-index, citation, g-index, m-index) should be used rather than relying on alphabetical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit tie-breaking rules and justification; encourage comparing discrepancies between production and citation rankings (and explain large rank shifts) to surface insights about productivity vs impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SCP and MCP for country production analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For country production, apply single-country production (SCP) and multiple-country production (MCP) metrics to distinguish domestic and international contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authors report and interpret SCP and MCP separately and justify how they aggregate or compare country-level outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide which structural analyses are necessary given objectives and field maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual, intellectual, and social structure analyses are key components, but authors may choose which to perform based on research objectives and the maturity of the field (e.g., social structure might be unnecessary for very recent/emerging topics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should judge whether the chosen combination of analyses aligns with study aims and field development; ask authors to justify excluding particular analyses when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual structure — keyword selection standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: In co-occurrence (conceptual) analysis, reviewers should assess how authors standardized keywords and eliminated redundancies (synonyms and variations), the criteria guiding the selection of keyword types (author keyword vs keyword plus), and how thresholds for keyword selection were determined and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require documentation of cleaning/normalization steps, clear criteria for choosing keyword sources, and justification (or sensitivity analysis) for threshold settings to reduce selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual structure — network visualization quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how effectively the visualization represents distinct clusters and what methods were used to label and interpret each cluster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for clear labeling methods, explanation of color/size/edge encodings, and narrative interpretation linking clusters to substantive themes rather than leaving visualizations uninterpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual structure — network density and centrality interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how central and peripheral concepts are differentiated and how relationships within and between clusters are analyzed (network density, centrality metrics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require authors to explain the meaning of centrality/density measures used, identify core vs peripheral concepts, and analyze inter-cluster relationships rather than merely reporting metric values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic map — contextual interpretation of automatic categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliometric software classifies themes (motor, niche, emerging/declining, basic) automatically; authors should interpret these categories rather than only presenting the thematic map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask authors to justify thematic labels, explain why a theme is considered emerging/declining, and connect map categories to contextual knowledge of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic evolution — justify time segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must provide logical reasoning for chosen time slices for thematic evolution (e.g., Sankey flows or progression maps) and ensure periods align with significant development trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should demand alignment between temporal segmentation and known field events/developments and look for sensitivity analyses to different periodizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic evolution — continuity and causal interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include the evolution of keywords over time, discuss significant shifts, and explain why certain themes emerged or declined rather than only showing movements on a map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage causal/historical interpretation (policy changes, technological shifts, paradigm shifts) and linking thematic movement to external events or bibliometric indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual structure — citation selection comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: For co-citation and other intellectual analyses, reviewers should assess how comprehensive citation coverage is across sources and time periods and how influential works were identified and incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require transparency about inclusion/exclusion of cited sources, databases searched, time-window choices, and any thresholds used to select citations for network construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual structure — cluster definition and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate what methods were used to define and validate clusters and how cluster labels were determined and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for methodological details (clustering algorithm, parameter choices), validation approaches (e.g., stability analysis, expert validation), and clear rationale for label assignment beyond algorithmic output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual structure — alignment of key authors/papers with performance analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Check how the identified key authors and key papers align with performance analysis findings (e.g., citation/ranking results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require cross-checks between intellectual-structure outputs and performance metrics; discrepancies should be explained (e.g., classic papers highly cited but not central in recent networks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Historiography — chronological scope and turning points
rubrics_metrics.description: In historiographic analyses, the visualization should present clear time frames that capture movements in research focus and discuss any turning points that shifted directions or triggered new branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ask authors to justify chronological granularity, point out and explain major turning points, and relate these to citation or publication evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historiography — explain absent influential papers
rubrics_metrics.description: If certain influential papers from performance analysis do not appear in historiography/co-citation maps, authors should provide an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request reasoning for absences (data coverage, thresholding, disciplinary differences) and consider whether methodological choices caused omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social structure — scope and representativeness of networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how diverse the representation of authors is across affiliations and countries in co-authorship networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require reporting on sampling/coverage biases, proportion of missing author affiliation data, and considerations of underrepresented regions or institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social structure — centrality, connectivity, and isolated clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine how central authors are identified, how inter-cluster connections are analyzed and represented, and how isolated clusters (or lack of connections) are explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explain centrality metrics, demonstrate how bridges/connectors are identified, and discuss causes/implications of isolated clusters (e.g., disciplinary silos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social structure — institutional collaboration analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether authors adequately identify key institutions, their contributions, and whether they emphasize long-lasting or emerging collaborations between institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for measures of institutional influence, temporal patterns of institutional collaborations, and interpretation of geographic/regional concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social structure — country collaboration and policy/geopolitical implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how regional and global collaboration dynamics are analyzed, whether dominant and emerging countries are identified, and whether implications for policy, funding, or geopolitics are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage discussion of how collaboration trends affect research capacity, funding strategies, and geopolitical influences; request explicit consideration of regional imbalances and political context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of performance analysis and science mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Review how effectively studies combine performance analysis (e.g., citations, productivity) with science mapping (conceptual/intellectual/social) to present a holistic view of the research landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require methodological alignment (temporal and granularity), explicit cross-validation between approaches, and demonstration that integration yields insights not visible in separate analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate author impact through multiple lenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive evaluation of author influence should consider both quantitative metrics and network positions (e.g., centrality, bridging roles) to reveal nuanced patterns beyond simple rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether studies identify bridge authors, rising scholars (increasing centrality vs citations), established researchers with declining centrality, and provide explanations for these patterns and their implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-validate research trends across indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure alignment between citation patterns and temporal thematic evolution; when misalignments occur, authors should explain them thoughtfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require checks that highly cited papers correspond to major nodes/themes in co-citation or thematic maps; if not, demand plausible explanations (e.g., citation time lag, interdisciplinary citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret geographic and institutional metrics alongside networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Country- and institution-level citation metrics should be interpreted together with collaboration network positions to reveal how knowledge flows and institutional roles interact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage joint presentation of performance and network indicators (e.g., high citations but peripheral collaboration) and discussion of causes and policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological alignment and robustness in integration
rubrics_metrics.description: When integrating analyses, assess temporal alignment between methods, handling of granularity differences, and treatment of methodological challenges such as citation time lags and variation across traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require sensitivity analyses, clear documentation of temporal windows, and justification for combining indicators with different accumulation dynamics; robustness of conclusions depends on addressing these challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore and explain contradictions rather than gloss over them
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies should investigate apparent contradictions between analyses (e.g., high citation counts but low network centrality) as they often reveal important field dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ask authors to treat contradictions as analytic opportunities, provide interpretations, and discuss implications for theory, policy, or future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for data source limitations and coverage differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize limitations of data sources (Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar) due to coverage patterns and indexing policies, which affect bibliometric results, especially for regional and emerging-field analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require authors to state database selection rationale, discuss coverage biases, and consider triangulating across sources or acknowledging limitations for certain regions/fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider citation dynamics and field-specific accumulation patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of field-specific citation behaviors and citation inflation over time (e.g., life sciences accumulate citations faster than social sciences), which affect interpretation of impact metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for field-normalized indicators, time-window choices that reflect accumulation rates, and caveats when comparing fields with different citation dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious when evaluating interdisciplinary research
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional bibliometric methods may undervalue interdisciplinary work due to smaller citation communities and delayed recognition; reviewers should account for this when judging impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage use of alternative indicators, longer time windows, and qualitative corroboration (expert judgment) when assessing interdisciplinary contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt VALOR-like framework for transparency and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a systematic approach (e.g., the VALOR framework) to ensure quality and transparency when dealing with multiple data sources and analytical tools, interpreting data in context and documenting limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require comprehensive documentation: data sources, extraction steps, preprocessing, parameter choices, temporal alignment, validation steps, reproducibility protocols, and clear discussion of limitations and strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate qualitative methods and advanced tools to enrich interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine bibliometric analyses with qualitative insights (expert interviews, case studies, content analysis) and consider advances in machine learning and NLP to improve keyword extraction and network mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage multimethod approaches to provide richer interpretation and suggest exploring ML/NLP for better term extraction, real-time trend detection, and reducing manual bias.
